title: Boss (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Boss (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - boss - lead 
 lead : A **boss** is a powerful, non-respawning enemy in *Dark Souls II*. Bosses are distinguishable from normal enemies as their name and health are displayed at the bottom of the screen once encountered, and they are usually on the opposite side of a white fog door.

In addition to bosses, there are a number of enemies that don't respawn upon death and are sometimes referred to as *minibosses*.

Unlike the bosses found in *Dark Souls*, the majority of bosses found in *Dark Souls II* can be considered optional, due to the Shrine of Winter's flexible requirements for passing. The list of bosses below is treated under the assumption that the player takes the most linear route, collecting the four Lord Souls, and at least passes through each major location.

title: Boss (Dark Souls II)
snippet: In addition to the main game, there are three additional downloadable content purchases that add additional areas and bosses to the game. The bosses for each area are listed as optional or not based on the need to defeat them for completion of the DLC.

title: Heide Greatlance
snippet:
Heide Greatlance -  Dark Souls II - weapon - description 
 description : A lance originating in Heide. A special alloy makes it very durable. The tip of the lance has been extended.

The composition of the alloy of these lances remains a mystery, but in Drangleic the attempt to imitate it resulted in the similar bradden steel.

Lances are normally wielded by mounted knights, and it takes considerable training to handle one on the ground.

title: Heide Greatlance
snippet:
Heide Greatlance -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Heide Greatlance is quite a powerful weapon when it is obtained, and hits very hard when fully upgraded. Its running attack is very effective when executed correctly; however, this attack consumes a large amount of stamina and durability. This weapon may be hard to use in PvP, as it's fairly easy to dodge the relatively narrow hitbox of its attacks. However, it can deal outstanding damage, should the attacks connect.

Players with high Faith should consider a Lightning Infusion for the Heide Greatlance as it will maintain its Strength and Dexterity scaling while increasing the C scaling in Lightning to a B at high reinforcement. Infusion will also cause a minimal reduction in physical damage, but this penalty is much smaller than most other weapons, and is well worth the large damage boost from Faith.

title: Heide Knight
snippet:
Heide Knight -  Dark Souls II - enemy - lead 
 lead : **Heide Knights** are enemies in *Dark Souls II*.

In the original version of the game, they are non-respawning, although they do so in *Scholar of the First Sin*. They are neutral until provoked, at which point they take a second to stand up before attacking; the areas in which they are found are completely different between the original release and *SotFS*.

title: Heide Knight
snippet:
Heide Knight -  Dark Souls II - enemy - notes 
 notes : The Heide Knights can be seen as counterparts to the Black Knights of *Dark Souls*, as they do not respawn and are few in number. However, the Heide Knights are far less aggressive, as they only attack the player after being provoked.
Heide Knights are guaranteed, at least in NG, to drop their weapons.
The Heide Knights can be both backstabbed and parried.
If the player decides to fight the Heide Knight in the Forest of Fallen Giants, it is recommended to kill all nearby Hollow Infantry in the area, including the archer. Otherwise, the smaller enemies may take the player by surprise and surround them.
If a guard break is used on a non-hostile knight, he will stand up and begin to wander about without turning hostile. This is fixed in *Scholar of the First Sin*, where they will immediately aggro upon rising to their feet.

snippet:

 attacks : **Swipe**: Swipes one of his arms across the arena, sometimes followed up by an overhead slam or another swipe with the opposite arm. Can be avoided by rolling towards it.

**Slam**: Performs an overhead slam, sometimes done with both hands, sometimes followed by another slam or a swipe. Can be avoided with a well-timed roll, or by sprinting left or right.

**Dive**: The Old Iron King dives into the molten iron, splashing some of it onto the arena in the process. After a short time, he will re-emerge in a different location, splashing additional iron onto the arena.

**Laser**: Charges his right hand with a fiery glow and shoots out a laser-like beam of Fire. Goes through walls. Can be avoided by sprinting left or right, or by rolling with good timing.

snippet:
Old Iron King -  Dark Souls II - boss - general_information 
 general_information : Located in Iron Keep, the Old Iron King is the final boss of this area who possesses one of the four great souls. He takes the form of a giant horned and winged monster, with rivulets of iron pouring from its body. The closest bonfire is near turtles and called Eygil's Idol.

title: Old Iron King
snippet:
Old Iron King -  Dark Souls II - boss - fight_overview 
 fight_overview : The fight is very simple and is similar to Ceaseless Discharge from the original *Dark Souls*. The main difference being the absence of any easy trick to defeat the King.

The player has little room to maneuver around the area, and may walk off or be thrown off the edge, causing an instant death. Due to his well-telegraphed attacks and long recovery times, there will be many openings for both healing and dealing damage. This means that the small area often becomes the main obstacle in this fight.

title: Old Iron King
snippet:
Old Iron King -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : The Old Iron King began his days as the Prince of Alken, a little-known and unestablished lord, with a lust for power and glory. He was later wed to the princess Mytha, but secretly had an affair with the Princess of Venn. To keep their secret, they built two twin bell towers, and created bell keepers and guardians to protect the bell towers from intruders, showing great knowledge in the art of golemcrafting.

title: Old Iron King
snippet: The Iron King would at some point trying to control the soul residing into the lava where the Iron Keep was built. He therefore immersed the Smelter Demon in the lava trying to infuse it with the soul lurking beneath, but when the iron golem was possessed, it struck down the king, and the lava raged sunking the Iron Keep. The King was then possessed by the evil that lurked below the magma, and his body then became molten earth.

title: Old Iron King
snippet:
Old Iron King -  Dark Souls II - boss - lead 
 lead : The **Old Iron King** (鉄の古王) is a boss in *Dark Souls II*.

title: Old Iron King
snippet:
**Laser**: Charges his right hand with a fiery glow and shoots out a laser-like beam of Fire. Goes through walls. Can be avoided by sprinting left or right, or by rolling with good timing.

**Fiery overhead slam**: Similar to the slam, the King performs an overhead slam, but will charge his hands with fire before smashing down onto the arena, causing pillars of fire to erupt from his hands. Should be avoided by sprinting away, as simply rolling may lead to players being hit with the fire.

**Flame Breath**: Shoots a line of fire out of his mouth. Can be rolled through, or side-stepped.

**Swiping Flames**: Shoots flames out of mouth in a wide arc. Can be avoided by rolling, or by keeping a safe distance away from the King. Alternatively, it is possible to walk in between the flames, although it can be very difficult to do.

**Roar**: Lets out a roar that releases a medium range area of effect explosion, similar to Wrath of the Gods. Usually only done if a player gets extremely close.

title: Old Iron King
snippet:
One must be cautious of the hole right next to the entrance, as it's possible to get knocked into it and die.

The best time to land high damage is when the boss slams his fist(s) into the ground and when he is using a flame attack. It is more difficult for pure melee players to hit the Old Iron King during a fire attack, but it is possible nonetheless. Damaging his horns seem to do extra damage as well and if the player can they should attack his hand while he is breathing fire.

Players would do well to take their time with this boss. One should not attempt to rush the battle and waste stamina before it is needed. Most of the Old Iron King's projected attacks drain high amounts of stamina, usually not allowing a player to stand more than one instance of an attack while blocking.

title: Old Iron King
snippet:
Old Iron King -  Dark Souls II - boss - strategy 
 strategy : All of the Old Iron King's attacks should be dodged, since being hit by them can be devastating and there's a possibility of being knocked off the edge, into an instant death.

There is a small area in the rightmost portion of the stage where one can go to avoid his sweeping flame breath if the player is not confident with rolling. Ranged characters can also set up there, if another player can draw aggro from them. Be careful, though, as the structure does not block the beam the Old Iron King fires from his right hand. Standing there for too long will also prompt the King to dive below the surface, emerging close to the player's position. The King will attempt to surface as close to the player as possible, preferably from behind the back. This can be manipulated to force surfacing in a particular location by running there immediately after the dive and facing away from the direction you would like him to surface.

title: Old Iron King
snippet: The Iron King was later approached by Sir Alonne, a great warrior from the east, who trained the King's soldiers and helped him forge a kingdom for himself from the old Kingdom of Venn. Doing so cost the Iron King what little resources he had, but in the process, he discovered an iron-producing miracle, which allowed him to freely shape and harness the powers of iron. With this new power, the Old Iron King became extremely wealthy and powerful, forging from iron both his entire castle, and various golems such as the Ironclads and the Smelter Demons. title: Shrine of Winter
snippet:
Shrine of Winter -  Dark Souls II - location - overview 
 overview : The Shrine of Winter is a small area leading to the steps of Drangleic Castle. It is found in the Shaded Woods by taking the left path at the Ruined Fork Road bonfire and is initially blocked by a door that demands a number of strong souls to open.

The door can be opened in one of two ways. The first is by defeating the four Old Ones: The Lost Sinner, Old Iron King, The Rotten, and The Duke's Dear Freja. This is the most linear option and will ensure most prior areas are visited beforehand, leading to the possibility of more loot and souls.

The second is by accumulating more than one million Soul Memory in a single New Game cycle. This requirement increases by an additional one million souls per New Game cycle, requiring the player to obtain two million souls after starting NG+, three million after starting NG++, and so on.

title: Shrine of Winter
snippet: Offline players may find a few good farming spots and use particular equipment to maximize their soul gain maximum. The Iron Keep is an excellent location and can easily yield 30,000 souls and more by progressing from the first bonfire to the Belfry Sol bonfire while wearing the Covetous Silver Serpent Ring +1 and the Jester's Gloves. Having some magic spells such as Great Heavy Soul Arrow will make this far easier as well as being able to kill the Alonne Knight Captains on the lower levels at the start. It is also best to pull the lever twice and then step on the pads to drop the knights into the lava instead of getting tangled up fighting them.

title: Shrine of Winter
snippet:
Shrine of Winter -  Dark Souls II - location - strategy 
 strategy : Obtaining one million souls is not as hard as it sounds; most players will earn this amount naturally over the course of one playthrough and may even reach it before beating any of the Old Ones. Playing online as a white phantom is a good way of earning souls; defeating bosses will usually earn players a few thousand or more.

title: Shrine of Winter
snippet:
This can be done twelve times before enemies stop respawning. Of course, confident players can also purchase a Bonfire Ascetic from Stone Trader Chloanne and continue to farm until the respawn limit is reached once again. Although, simply using the Company of Champions Covenant is not only safer, it also factors out the huge damage increases; the only down side is the soul gains stay the same meaning the player would need to farm for longer. It is up to the player to decide which is better.

By following this strategy, the player also has the added bonus of possibly finding Large Titanite Shards dropped by the Old Ironclad Soldiers and the armor dropped by the Alonne Knight Captains which can then be sold to Lonesome Gavlan for a small margin as well. The Covetous Gold Serpent Ring +1 and the Jester's Cap, both obtained from Magerold of Lanafir in the same area, will prove useful in this endeavor.

title: The Rotten
snippet:
The Rotten -  Dark Souls II - boss - fight_overview 
 fight_overview : Throughout the fight, the Rotten alternates between his cleaver and his empty hand. His cleaver deals heavy damage and can send the player flying or easily stun-lock the player and break their guard. The hand has two moves; a front smash and a grab. The grab damages twice; the initial damage is from the grab itself and the following damage comes when the Rotten wrings the player out like a rag.

title: The Rotten
snippet:
After losing about half of its health, the Rotten begins using ranged attacks that deal heavy dark damage. One travels in a straight line after a heavy downward slash, while the other is an area of effect attack. The Rotten will be vulnerable for a short time after each attack, giving ample time to switch to offense. With the Old Leo Ring and a thrusting weapon equipped, this fight can end soon after.

Dealing enough damage to one of the arms will sever it, but it will regenerate after some time. If the player cuts off the left arm, they will be rewarded with a Lockstone.

With magic, the player should keep their distance from the Rotten and only cast while the Rotten recovers from its attacks.

title: Crown of the Ivory King
snippet:
Crown of the Ivory King -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - access

The Frozen Flower is granted upon loading and is required to open the door to Frozen Eleum Loyce. In the Scholar of the First Sin edition, the Frozen Flower is instead found in Drangleic Castle.

title: The Lost Crowns
snippet:
The Lost Crowns -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - requirements 
 requirements : There are no requirements to access the DLC, other than having access to the Primal Bonfire or location where the warp shrine is located. Each warp shrine leads to a cavernous room containing a locked door.

Players who own the DLC will receive a key item that will allow them to open the door. Players who don't own the DLC are still able to play through parts of the new content, but only as a summoned phantom.

title: Crown of the Sunken King
snippet:
Crown of the Sunken King -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - access

This changes in the *Scholar of the First Sin* edition of the game; the Dragon Talon can be found on a body behind the 'Forgotten Door' unlocked with the Forgotten Key, at the bottom of the well in Majula. This door grants access to Shulva, Sanctum City.

title: Dragon Shrine
snippet:
Dragon Shrine -  Dark Souls II - location - plot

SotFS: Located just past the Shaded Ruins bonfire. Upon exiting the ruined structure, it is to the left in a metal chest. The chest is blocked by a petrified Lion Warrior, and there are several curse jars nearby.

title: Frozen Flower

title: Crown of the Old Iron King
snippet:
Crown of the Old Iron King -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - access 
 access : To access the content, defeat the Old Iron King in Iron Keep and proceed to the Primal Bonfire. Use the altar behind the bonfire to travel to the starting area. Upon loading, the Heavy Iron Key will be added to the player's inventory, which grants access to Brume Tower.

This changes in the *Scholar of the First Sin* edition of the game; the Heavy Iron Key can be found inside of the door opened by the Iron Key, near The Last Giant's boss room in the Forest of Fallen Giants.

title: Illusory Ring of the Exalted
snippet:
Illusory Ring of the Exalted -  Dark Souls II - ring - strategy 
 strategy : By using soul-giving items to get one million souls, one can instantly pass the door at the Shrine of Winter and go to Drangleic Castle at the start of the game. This saves the player a lot of work, as only seven bosses will be *required* to beat the game.

A relatively easy way to acquire this ring, for magic users, is to wait until the first New Game Plus cycle to attempt the run. Prior to passing into NG+, attune Repair, any variant of Heal, and any other magic one desires, then wear the Crown of the Old Iron King to restore casts. Repair and Heal removes the two most common needs to rest at a bonfire, making the challenge a matter of patience.

title: Pilgrims of Dark
snippet:
Pilgrims of Dark -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : Players must talk to Darkdiver Grandahl in three separate locations:
#Shaded Woods: From the Shaded Ruins bonfire, advance forward until an open area is reached. Start walking right and past the two towers that lead to Scorpioness Najka. There will be a boarded up hole in the nearby grassy area by the cliff, which will let the player drop down to Grandahl. To break it, the player must simply walk over it.
#Black Gulch: Dropping down from the cliff near the two Razorback Nightcrawlers will land the player on a ledge with a locked door. To obtain the key for it, drop down two more times into an enclave that houses two Elite Giants; killing them will grant the Forgotten Key, along with a Soul of a Giant.

title: Shrine of Amana
snippet:
Shrine of Amana -  Dark Souls II - location - notes 
 notes : There is a shrine located above the last bonfire. The player must be hollow and have talked to all of the Milfanito to unlock the door. This shrine can be used to reverse hollowing, but only if the player has no Human Effigies in their inventory or storage and is not a sinner.
The Shrine of Amana is a good location to farm Twinkling Titanite because it drops from most enemies. Equipment that raises item discovery is recommended. It's easier to start farming runs from the third bonfire.

title: Frigid Outskirts
snippet:
Frigid Outskirts -  Dark Souls II - location - overview 
 overview : The location can only be accessed after unlocking the door in front of the Expulsion Chamber bonfire using the Garrison Ward Key. Inside is a coffin that can be used to slide down the icy slopes and into the Frigid Outskirts. Once there, severe blizzards will begin to cycle every few moments, which inhibits the player's vision and cause Ice Stallions to spawn at random.

The goal is to reach the dwelling of Lud and Zallen, the king's pets, who are found in a pit some distance away. Along the way are various enemies who will attack and dilapidated buildings that contain loot.

Once at the outskirts, one cannot return to Frozen Eleum Loyce by normal means. The player must use a warping item or spell, die or make use of the warp point provided after killing the area bosses.

 how_to_join : Players may join the Way of White by talking either to Petrus at the Firelink Shrine or Reah after you have rescued her from the Tomb of the Giants.

The Chosen Undead may choose to perpetuate the Age of Fire, or instead bring about the Age of Dark. There are no other requirements, aside from defeating the final boss, to access either ending.

snippet:
Sweet Shalquoir -  Dark Souls II - character - plot 
 plot : Found in a house in Majula, Sweet Shalquoir is a talking cat who acts similar to Oswald of Carim of *Dark Souls* in the way that she manages the player's covenants. Whilst talking to her, the player can view their current covenant rank and other covenant managing options.

title: Boss Soul Items (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Boss Soul Items (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - notes 
 notes : Once Ludleth dies in the ritual to access the Kiln of the First Flame, the player may access soul transposition by interacting with his ashes. However, this will only work if he was given the Transposing Kiln prior to the ritual, if this is not the case then the transposition service will remain unavailable for the remainder of the playthrough.
When in possession of both Lothric's Holy Sword and Lorian's Greatsword, talking to Ludleth will unlock the option to combine the two into the Twin Princes' Greatsword through dialogue. This will consume the two weapons in the process at no soul cost.

title: Silverblack Shield

Silverblack Shield -  Dark Souls II - shield - description 
 description : A silver-black shield imbued with the power of dark.

The equipment of the wardens of the Undead Crypt are soaked in its darkness, and permeated by its power. The grave wardens are said to know the name of every guest who rests in the crypt, no matter how long they have been with them.

 how_to_join : The covenant item is received by talking to Horace the Hushed at the Halfway Fortress bonfire in the Road of Sacrifices, or at Firelink Shrine after defeating the Deacons of the Deep. He will also drop the item if he is killed.

Heirs of the Sun -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - how_to_join

snippet:
Brotherhood of Blood -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : Talk to Titchy Gren, located in the Undead Purgatory directly after the Executioner's Chariot boss fight. title: Karla
snippet:
Karla -  Dark Souls III - character - location 
 location : Karla is located in a locked cell in the lower level of the Irithyll Dungeon, in the area with numerous Jailers. In order to unlock it, the player must have the Jailer's Key Ring, found in the Profaned Capital, and then go back to the Irithyll Dungeon once more to free her.

After exhausting her dialogue and agreeing to rescue her, Karla will relocate to Firelink Shrine and become a merchant there. She can be found under the stairs to the left of Andre's smithy. Unlike most Firelink Shrine characters, she has no questline, nor does she relocate after all of her wares have been purchased, and will remain in Firelink Shrine regardless of the player's actions unless killed.

title: Equipment (Dark Souls II)

title: Merchant (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Merchant (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - character - lead 
 lead : **Merchants** are characters in *Dark Souls III* that trade in various goods, such as items, spells, and armor.

Some merchants are available from the start of the game, while others must be located throughout the world and brought back to Firelink Shrine, with the exception of Patches, who may sell items once discovered in the Cathedral of the Deep.

Unlike the previous games, all merchants (with the exception of Ludleth of Courland) are capable of selling and buying items and equipment.

Merchants will increase their stock of sold goods once specific requirements are met.

title: Vince of Thorolund
snippet:
Vince of Thorolund -  Dark Souls - character - plot 
 plot : Vince and Nico are the bodyguards of Reah of Thorolund. He will appear with his companions in the Firelink Shrine after the player beats the Capra Demon in the Lower Undead Burg. Unlike his mumbling companion, Vince will have a brief conversation with the player. In it, he tells the player that his party are going on a quest, but reveals little more.

If the player does not exhaust all of his and Reah's dialogue, they will leave Firelink Shrine when the player defeats Pinwheel in The Catacombs.

The player next encounters Vince and Nico as Hollowed enemies in the Tomb of the Giants, in the pit that Patches kicks them into. The player must defeat them in order to rescue Reah.

title: Petrus of Thorolund
snippet:
After the Capra Demon in the lower Undead Burg is defeated, Petrus is joined by Reah of Thorolund and two companions from the Thorolund Order (named Vince and Nico) in the Firelink Shrine. They are on a secret mission and will not talk much about what is going on. Once the game has been reloaded or the player leaves Firelink Shrine, the visitors will be gone and Petrus will not talk much about what happened.

If the player talks to Lautrec of Carim he will offer information to the player for souls based upon level. He tells the player about how the lady and two companions went down to The Catacombs and got attacked, while Petrus escaped and left the others behind. If the player talks to Petrus after this, he will tell his side of the story and about how the lady is left alone and her companions have been turned to hollow.

Talking to Oswald of Carim will result in some implications and accusations against Petrus, claiming that his soul is drenched in sin.

title: Darkwraith (covenant)
snippet:
Darkwraith (covenant) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - requirements 
 requirements : The player must place the Lordvessel for Kaathe instead of Frampt. The player could also speak to Kaathe and choose the "warp" option. After arriving at Firelink Altar, the player can then, instead of placing the Lordvessel, return to the Abyss and join the covenant while still keeping both serpents in the player's service.

title: Warrior of Sunlight
snippet:
Warrior of Sunlight -  Dark Souls - mechanic - requirements 
 requirements : The player must have 25 (50 in the non-patched version) Faith. This requirement is lowered by 5 for every boss the player kills as a white phantom.

title: Princess's Guard
snippet:
Princess's Guard -  Dark Souls - mechanic - requirements 
 requirements : The player must not have dispelled the illusion of Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight.
